title: I am the gate (John 10:1–10)
hookLine: I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly

lines: A STONE CIRCLE ON A HILLSIDE.
cards: A sheepfold on a hillside: a rough circle of stone walls, chest high, with one gap for an opening. At night the sheep are led inside, safe from wolves and thieves.

Jesus is still talking to the listeners who threw the healed man out. He tells them a picture-story: sheep, a gatekeeper, thieves who climb over the wall, and a shepherd who walks in through the door.
John says plainly they didn't understand it. So Jesus tries again, more directly.

teach.h: HE CALLS HIS SHEEP BY NAME.
teach.b: First, the shepherd. The sheep hear his voice, and "he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out." Not a herd.
Names. Then the surprise: "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture." The King James says door; some modern Bibles say gate.
Either way, it's the opening in the wall.

teach.h: BREAD, LIGHT, AND NOW THE DOOR.
teach.b: John has given us I am sayings before: bread, light. Now, the way in. People often tell how a shepherd in that region might lie down across the gap at night, so nothing could get in or out without stepping over him.
Whether or not every shepherd did that, it's a good picture of what Jesus is saying. And look at the words: go in and out. A gate isn't only for locking in.

teach.h: IN TO REST, OUT TO PASTURE.
teach.b: In, to rest at night. Out, to pasture in the morning.
Then the verse behind today's line: "The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly."
The Greek word behind abundantly means more than enough, overflowing. Not just getting by.
Life with something left over. Christians often hold this line as a picture of what faith is meant to be: not a smaller life fenced in by rules, but a bigger one, with a safe place to come home to.

how: Christians often quote John 10:10 when describing the life they hope faith brings.

p: calls his own sheep by name
comes to steal, kill and destroy
an I am, after bread and light
safety at night, pasture by day

it says "I am the door." some modern Bibles say gate.
Jesus's listeners understood the sheepfold story right away

the word for abundantly means more than enough

games.q: you're a sheep in the fold. morning comes and the gate opens. what does the story say happens?
o: you stay inside, where it's safe.
you go out and find pasture.
games.why: the sheep "shall go in and out, and find pasture." the gate is for safety and for freedom.

practice: Think of your day as it's going to go, how much of it is errands, emails, just getting through; that's real, and it's fine.
Now picture one small thing that's more than necessary, a longer walk, a real conversation, cooking something properly, ten minutes outside, music you love played loud, and choose one.
If you pray, give thanks for the life you have and ask for it in full; if not, just savor the thing you chose.

wordCard.voice: Sheepfold. The walled hillside pen Jesus pictures, with one gap for a gate: the shepherd leads his sheep in to rest, and out to pasture.
